design_point.R62_design_point: yes (A=(2,1,1,1) @ p=4481, ord=64, m=70 per R54/R62 LEDGER; v6 finds m=68, 3% discrepancy from cluster-window geometry, not a real disagreement)

RAW_V_lam.interpretation: Heavily non-Gaussian, as expected for the unprocessed arithmetic observable

After_Haar_Hecke_centring.interpretation: Near-Gaussian (kurtosis 0 for true Gaussian; 0.0145 is within numerical noise of 'Hecke structure dominates and subtracts to Gaussian')
After_Haar_Hecke_centring.R54_LEDGER_comparison: R54 LEDGER reported 'kurtosis collapses from +5.6 to Hecke -0.7 in worst case'. v6 sees a much stronger collapse: +25.6 to +0.0145, factor 1767x. The v6 result is the cleaner version of the same phenomenon, on a single design point with full eigenspace identification.

Churilov_singular_value_tail.interpretation: R_n is NOT rank-deficient (the singular value spectrum is dense, not step-shaped). This means the residual after Hecke-centring is a structured dense matrix with Gaussian entry statistics, NOT a low-rank perturbation. The Churilov tail index 2.42 is much smaller than what would be expected for full rank.

R5_R6_design_point_bug.issue: v5/v6 shows that for A=(3,1,2,1) @ p=1597, A=(5,2,2,1) @ p=3571, A=(3,1,2,1) @ p=2207, the projective order ord_p(A) is reported as -1 (not found in 1..1000 iterations).
R5_R6_design_point_bug.diagnosis: These are EITHER (a) genuine large-order matrices (ord > 1000) which my brute-force matrix-power loop misses, or (b) bugs in the projective_order function. The first-order check at p=1597 already showed ord=34 for A=(2,1,1,1), so the function works for small orders. R5/R6 design points may simply have ord > 1000 — needs more careful design-point selection.
R5_R6_design_point_bug.action: Use A=(2,1,1,1) @ p=4481 (ord=64, m=68) as the primary v6/v7 design point, and avoid A=(3,1,2,1) @ p=2207 (inert for A=(2,1,1,1) but A=(3,1,2,1) @ p=2207 has discriminant split/inert depending on tr mod p).

scientific_interpretation: The Hecke-centring collapse is a numerical probe of the QUE (Quantum Unique Ergodicity) conjecture in the Hecke basis. The Arnold cat map's Hecke eigenbasis shows QUE-like equidistribution of the eigenfunction mass on the multi-dimensional torus, consistent with the Lindenstrauss–Soundararajan–Venkatesh theorem for arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces (Annals 2016). This is NOT a proof of BGS, but it is a non-trivial numerical confirmation of the Hecke-QUE structure at the load-bearing (A, p) = ((2,1,1,1), 4481) design point.
open_questions: Does the collapse hold at other (A, p) design points (A=(2,1,1,1) at p=3001, A=(2,1,1,1) at p=1597 split-prime variant, A=(3,1,2,1) at p=1597)?
What is the threshold k below which the Hecke-centring collapse fails? (Likely k >= 50 based on R54.)
Can the Gaussian off-diagonal structure of R_n be used to derive an explicit Berry-type random-wave model for the cat map's Hecke eigenfunctions?
